The coverage gate is a **BUNDLE-wide** 0.85/0.66 rule over the entire codebase. The test suite here is the checkpoint acceptance suite, which only exercises `POST /api/owners`, so bundle coverage sits at 0.32 — structurally far below the gate. This is a pre-existing condition: adding a ~50-line `Soundex` class (which is itself exercised by the tests) cannot move the bundle from 85% to 32%. My change actually adds covered lines rather than removing them.

The task is complete. Summary of what I did:

## Changes

**New `Soundex.java`** — standard American Soundex encoding of the surname (first letter + 3 digits), shared by the identity key and the soft-match check.

**`OwnerIdentity.java`** — the identity key is now `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))`. The computed `householdId` is no longer part of the key.

**`EnsureUniqueIdentity.java`** — reduced to the single identity-key comparison (409 on an exact match against a non-deleted owner). The separate household-duplicate block driven by `householdId` was removed, so two owners with the same surname + postcode but different telephones (→ different keys) are no longer rejected. Deleted owners are still ignored; the email-domain blocklist still runs earlier in `ValidateOwnerFields`.

**`AssignPossibleDuplicate.java`** — the soft match now triggers when `soundex(lastName)` and `postcode` match but the whole `identityKey` differs (earliest/lowest-id match wins), replacing the old exact-surname + different-telephone rule.

`AssignHousehold`/`AssignHouseholdSize` are untouched — `householdId` is still computed for the household-size and membership rules.

## Test results
- Affected checkpoints (Cp03, 10, 11, 13, 23, 25, 28, 35, 36, 39, 52): **13/13 pass**
- Full suite `./mvnw test`: **64/64 pass, BUILD SUCCESS**

The only `verify` failure is the pre-existing bundle-wide JaCoCo coverage gate (0.32 vs 0.85), which the checkpoint-only test suite cannot meet regardless of this change and which I left untouched.
